get.description: Retrieve a comprehensive list of all agreements overview with filtering options.

parameters.name: filter[client.id]
parameters.description:
Filters records by using a query string on the field `client.id`.

Supports comparison operators `eq`, `in`.

Operator semantics:

- `eq` — Exact match. Default when no operator prefix is supplied.
- `in` — Matches any value in a comma-separated list.

Query examples:

parameters.name: filter[client.id]
parameters.description:
Filters records by using a query string on the field `client.id`.

Supports comparison operators `eq`, `in`.

Operator semantics:

- `eq` — Exact match. Default when no operator prefix is supplied.
- `in` — Matches any value in a comma-separated list.

Query examples:

`filter[client.id]=0d3e7d0k-241a-461r-av15-758a90d70283`

`filter[client.id]=eq:0d3e7d0k-241a-461r-av15-758a90d70283`

`filter[client.id]=in:0d3e7d0k-241a-461r-av15-758a90d70283,1a2b3c4d-5e6f-7a8b-9c0d-e1f2a3b4c5d6`

parameters.name: filter[assigned_user_id]
parameters.description: Filter assessments to clients assigned to the supplied account-team users. Uses eq: for one user or in: for multiple users.

parameters.name: filter[title]
parameters.description:
Filters records by using a query string on the field `title`.

Supports comparison operators `eq`, `cont`.

Operator semantics:

- `eq` — Exact match. Default when no operator prefix is supplied.
- `cont` — Case-insensitive substring match (`LIKE %value%`). Use this for free-form search inputs; the supplied value is matched anywhere inside the field, and `%` / `_` characters in the value are escaped so they do not act as wildcards.

Query examples:

`filter[title]=example_string`

`filter[title]=eq:example_string`

`filter[title]=cont:exam`

parameters.name: filter[status]
parameters.description:
Filters records by using a query string on the field `status`.

Supports comparison operators `eq`, `in`.

Operator semantics:

- `eq` — Exact match. Default when no operator prefix is supplied.
- `in` — Matches any value in a comma-separated list.

Query examples:

`filter[status]=example_string`

`filter[status]=eq:example_string`

`filter[status]=in:example_string,another_string`

Available values: `Completed`, `InProgress`.

parameters.name: filter[assessment_template_id]
parameters.description:
Filters records by using a query string on the field `assessment_template_id`.

Supports comparison operators `eq`, `in`.

Operator semantics:

- `eq` — Exact match. Default when no operator prefix is supplied.
- `in` — Matches any value in a comma-separated list.

Query examples:

`filter[assessment_template_id]=example_string`

`filter[assessment_template_id]=in:example_string,another_string`

parameters.name: filter[score_max]

parameters.description:
Narrows the list to clients assigned to any of the supplied users. Use eq: for one user or in: for multiple users.
The reserved value none matches clients with no account team member, and can appear in an in: list alongside user ids to match either.

parameters.name: filter[source]
parameters.description: Narrows the list to clients with lineage from any supplied integration configuration. Use eq: for one source or in: for multiple sources.

parameters.name: filter[meeting_policy_status]
parameters.description: Filter clients by meeting-policy compliance. Use eq: for one status or in: for multiple statuses.

parameters.name: filter[segment_id]
parameters.description:
Filter clients by segment identifier. Use the eq: operator and repeat the parameter for multiple segments.
Use null:true to match clients with no segment; combining it with eq: values matches either.

parameters.name: filter[client_access_group_id]
parameters.description:
Filter clients by client access group identifier. Use the eq: operator and repeat the parameter for multiple groups.
Use null:true to match clients with no access group; combining it with eq: values matches either.

parameters.name: filter[vertical_id]
parameters.description:
Filter clients by vertical identifier. Use the eq: operator and repeat the parameter for multiple verticals.
Use null:true to match clients with no vertical; combining it with eq: values matches either.

parameters.name: filter[hardware_count]
parameters.description: Filter clients by their hardware asset count. Use eq: for an exact value, or repeat gte: and lte: bounds.

parameters.name: filter[software_count]
parameters.description: Filter clients by their software asset count. Use eq: for an exact value, or repeat gte: and lte: bounds.

parameters.name: filter[last_assessment_score]
parameters.description: Filter clients by last-assessment score percentage. Use eq: for an exact value, or repeat gte: and lte: bounds.

parameters.name: filter[last_assessment_days_ago]
parameters.description: Filter clients by the number of days since their last assessment. Use eq: for an exact value, or repeat gte: and lte: bounds.

parameters.name: filter[upcoming_meeting_days]
parameters.description: Filter clients by the number of days until their next meeting. Use eq: for an exact value, or repeat gte: and lte: bounds.

parameters.name: filter[last_meeting_starts_at]
parameters.description: Filter clients by the date of their most recent past meeting. Use eq: for an exact yyyy-MM-dd value, or repeat gte: and lte: bounds.

parameters.name: filter[license]
parameters.description: Filter clients by assigned license. Use the eq: operator with lmx or pro, or eq:null to match clients with no license.

get.description: List deliverables across the caller's account with optional client-scoped filtering, sorting, and cursor pagination.

parameters.name: filter[client.id]
parameters.description:
Filters records by using a query string on the field `client.id`.

Supports comparison operators `eq`, `in`.

Operator semantics:

- `eq` — Exact match. Default when no operator prefix is supplied.
- `in` — Matches any value in a comma-separated list.

Query examples:

`filter[client.id]=0d3e7d0k-241a-461r-av15-758a90d70283`

`filter[client.id]=eq:0d3e7d0k-241a-461r-av15-758a90d70283`

`filter[client.id]=in:0d3e7d0k-241a-461r-av15-758a90d70283,1a2b3c4d-5e6f-7a8b-9c0d-e1f2a3b4c5d6`

parameters.name: filter[status]
parameters.description:
Filters records by using a query string on the field `status`.

Supports comparison operators `eq`, `in`.

Operator semantics:

- `eq` — Exact match. Default when no operator prefix is supplied.
- `in` — Matches any value in a comma-separated list.

Query examples:

`filter[status]=example_string`

`filter[status]=eq:example_string`

`filter[status]=in:example_string,another_string`

Available values: `Published`, `Unpublished`.

parameters.name: filter[created_by]
parameters.description:
Filters records by using a query string on the field `created_by`.

Supports comparison operators `eq`, `in`.

Operator semantics:

- `eq` — Exact match. Default when no operator prefix is supplied.
- `in` — Matches any value in a comma-separated list.

Query examples:

`filter[created_by]=0d3e7d0k-241a-461r-av15-758a90d70283`

`filter[created_by]=eq:0d3e7d0k-241a-461r-av15-758a90d70283`

`filter[created_by]=in:0d3e7d0k-241a-461r-av15-758a90d70283,1a2b3c4d-5e6f-7a8b-9c0d-e1f2a3b4c5d6`

parameters.name: filter[has_meeting]
parameters.description:
Filters records by using a query string on the field `has_meeting`.

Supports comparison operators `eq`.

Operator semantics:

- `eq` — Exact match. Default when no operator prefix is supplied.

Query examples:

`filter[has_meeting]=true`

`filter[has_meeting]=eq:true`

parameters.name: filter[meeting.id]
parameters.description:
Filters records by using a query string on the field `meeting.id`.

Supports comparison operators `eq`.

Operator semantics:

- `eq` — Exact match. Default when no operator prefix is supplied.

Query examples:

`filter[meeting.id]=0d3e7d0k-241a-461r-av15-758a90d70283`

`filter[meeting.id]=eq:0d3e7d0k-241a-461r-av15-758a90d70283`

parameters.name: filter[name]
parameters.description:
Filters records by using a query string on the field `name`.

Supports comparison operators `eq`, `cont`.

Operator semantics:

- `eq` — Exact match. Default when no operator prefix is supplied.
- `cont` — Case-insensitive substring match (`LIKE %value%`). Use this for free-form search inputs; the supplied value is matched anywhere inside the field, and `%` / `_` characters in the value are escaped so they do not act as wildcards.

Query examples:

`filter[name]=example_string`

`filter[name]=eq:example_string`

`filter[name]=cont:exam`

parameters.name: filter[is_test]
parameters.description:
Filters records by using a query string on the field `is_test`.

Supports comparison operators `eq`, `in`.

Operator semantics:

- `eq` — Exact match. Default when no operator prefix is supplied.
- `in` — Matches any value in a comma-separated list.

Query examples:

`filter[is_test]=true`

`filter[is_test]=eq:true`

`filter[is_test]=in:true,false`

parameters.name: filter[type]
parameters.description:
Filters records by using a query string on the field `type`.

Supports comparison operators `eq`, `in`.

Operator semantics:

- `eq` — Exact match. Default when no operator prefix is supplied.
- `in` — Matches any value in a comma-separated list.

Query examples:

`filter[type]=example_string`

`filter[type]=eq:example_string`

`filter[type]=in:example_string,another_string`

Available values: `Custom`, `Template`.

parameters.name: filter[updated_at.gte]
parameters.description:
Filters records by using a query string on the field `updated_at.gte`.

Supports comparison operators `eq`, `gte`.

Operator semantics:

- `eq` — Exact match. Default when no operator prefix is supplied.
- `gte` — Greater than or equal to the supplied value.

Query examples:

`filter[updated_at.gte]=2025-11-11T15:30:00Z`

`filter[updated_at.gte]=eq:2025-11-11T15:30:00Z`

`filter[updated_at.gte]=gte:2025-11-11T15:30:00Z`

parameters.name: filter[updated_at.lte]

Filters records by using a query string on the field `updated_at.lte`.

Supports comparison operators `eq`, `lte`.

Operator semantics:

- `eq` — Exact match. Default when no operator prefix is supplied.
- `lte` — Less than or equal to the supplied value.

Query examples:

`filter[updated_at.lte]=2025-11-11T15:30:00Z`

`filter[updated_at.lte]=eq:2025-11-11T15:30:00Z`

`filter[updated_at.lte]=lte:2025-11-11T15:30:00Z`

parameters.name: filter[client.segment_id]
parameters.description:
Narrows results to clients in any supplied segment. Repeat eq: for each segment, or use in: with a
comma-separated list. Use null:true to match clients with no segment; combined with ids it matches either.

parameters.name: filter[client.vertical_id]
parameters.description:
Narrows results to clients in any supplied vertical. Repeat eq: for each vertical, or use in: with a
comma-separated list. Use null:true to match clients with no vertical; combined with ids it matches either.

parameters.name: filter[client.client_access_group_id]
parameters.description:
Narrows results to clients in any supplied client access group. Repeat eq: for each group, or use in: with
a comma-separated list. Use null:true to match clients with no access group; combined with ids it matches
either.

get.description: List all goals to help you quickly find relevant objectives with filtering options.

parameters.name: filter[is_archived]
parameters.description: When true, returns only archived goals. When omitted or false, returns only active goals.

parameters.name: filter[client.id]
parameters.description:
Filters records by using a query string on the field `client.id`.

Supports comparison operators `eq`, `in`.

Operator semantics:

- `eq` — Exact match. Default when no operator prefix is supplied.
- `in` — Matches any value in a comma-separated list.

Query examples:

`filter[client.id]=0d3e7d0k-241a-461r-av15-758a90d70283`

`filter[client.id]=eq:0d3e7d0k-241a-461r-av15-758a90d70283`

`filter[client.id]=in:0d3e7d0k-241a-461r-av15-758a90d70283,1a2b3c4d-5e6f-7a8b-9c0d-e1f2a3b4c5d6`

parameters.name: filter[title]
parameters.description:
Filters records by using a query string on the field `title`.

Supports comparison operators `eq`, `cont`.

Operator semantics:

- `eq` — Exact match. Default when no operator prefix is supplied.
- `cont` — Case-insensitive substring match (`LIKE %value%`). Use this for free-form search inputs; the supplied value is matched anywhere inside the field, and `%` / `_` characters in the value are escaped so they do not act as wildcards.

Query examples:

`filter[title]=example_string`

`filter[title]=eq:example_string`

`filter[title]=cont:exam`

parameters.name: filter[status]
parameters.description:
Filters records by using a query string on the field `status`.

Supports comparison operators `eq`, `in`.

Operator semantics:

- `eq` — Exact match. Default when no operator prefix is supplied.
- `in` — Matches any value in a comma-separated list.

Query examples:

`filter[status]=example_string`

`filter[status]=eq:example_string`

`filter[status]=in:example_string,another_string`

Available values: `AtRisk`, `Complete`, `OffTrack`, `OnHold`, `OnTrack`.

parameters.name: filter[assigned_user_id]
parameters.description: Narrows goals to clients assigned to any supplied user. Use eq: for one user or in: for multiple users.

parameters.name: filter[period.year]
parameters.description:
Filters records by using a query string on the field `period.year`.

Supports comparison operators `eq`.

Operator semantics:

- `eq` — Exact match. Default when no operator prefix is supplied.

get.description: Retrieve delivered Inbox notifications for the authenticated user, newest first. The default page size is 50 and the maximum is 200. The cursor is opaque; omit it for the first page and pass the next_cursor value from the previous response. Pagination is best effort and may skip or repeat records when the inbox changes. The optional search matches the actor name, the captured text, and the current record and client names, ignoring case and accents.

parameters.name: filter[read_state]
parameters.description: All delivered notifications, or only unread notifications. Defaults to All.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description:
Text to find in the actor name, the notification text, or the current record or client name, ignoring case and accents.
Leading and trailing whitespace is ignored and a blank value is the same as none. At most 200 characters.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: One or more sortable fields, separated by commas. Prefix with '+' to sort ascending or '-' to sort descending.

parameters.name: page_size
parameters.description: The number of records to be returned in a single page

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description:
Opaque cursor of the page to return. Omit this value for the first
page, then pass the next_cursor value from the previous response.
            
- Cursor pagination cannot guarantee atomicity.
- Endpoints may skip new records inserted between paginated reads.
- Endpoints may occasionally return duplicate records.

parameters.name: filter[is_archived]
parameters.description: When true, returns only archived initiatives. When omitted or false, returns only active initiatives.

parameters.description: Whether initiatives without a scheduled fiscal quarter are included when filtering by scheduled period. Defaults to false.

parameters.description: Whether initiatives marked internal are included. Defaults to true.

parameters.name: currency_scope
parameters.description: Currency used for calculated initiative values. Available values: client, account. Defaults to client.

parameters.name: filter[needs_attention]
parameters.description:
Filters records by using a query string on the field `needs_attention`.

Supports comparison operators `eq`.

Operator semantics:

- `eq` — Exact match. Default when no operator prefix is supplied.

Query examples:

`filter[needs_attention]=true`

`filter[needs_attention]=eq:true`

parameters.name: filter[client.id]
parameters.description:
Filters records by using a query string on the field `client.id`.

Supports comparison operators `eq`, `in`.

Operator semantics:

- `eq` — Exact match. Default when no operator prefix is supplied.
- `in` — Matches any value in a comma-separated list.

Query examples:

`filter[client.id]=0d3e7d0k-241a-461r-av15-758a90d70283`

`filter[client.id]=eq:0d3e7d0k-241a-461r-av15-758a90d70283`

`filter[client.id]=in:0d3e7d0k-241a-461r-av15-758a90d70283,1a2b3c4d-5e6f-7a8b-9c0d-e1f2a3b4c5d6`

parameters.name: filter[status]
parameters.description:
Filters records by using a query string on the field `status`.

Supports comparison operators `eq`, `in`.

get.description: List the hardware assets affected by an insight now or projected to be affected at a future date. Supports query filters, free-text search, pagination, and sorting. Only insights with a Hardware asset scope are supported.

parameters.name: insight_id
parameters.description: Identifier of the insight whose affected assets should be listed, as returned by the insights list endpoint.

parameters.name: insight_ids
parameters.description: Additional insight identifiers. Assets matching any selected insight are returned. A maximum of 50 additional insight identifiers can be provided per request.

parameters.name: forecast_days
parameters.description: Optional number of days into the future at which to evaluate the insight. When omitted, the endpoint returns assets affected today. A forecast includes assets already affected today when they are still expected to match at the future date.

parameters.name: exclude_currently_affected
parameters.description: When true, excludes assets affected today so the response contains only assets newly projected to match at the forecast date. Requires forecast_days.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Free-text search applied across the console's searchable fields.

parameters.name: client_id
parameters.description: Optional Core API client ID used to limit results to one client. Omit to search across accessible clients.

parameters.description: Number of records to return in a single page. Defaults to 50.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Cursor of the page to return. Omit for the first page, then pass the next_cursor value from the previous response.

get.description: Retrieve a comprehensive list of all client meetings with filtering options.

parameters.name: filter[client.id]
parameters.description:
Filters records by using a query string on the field `client.id`.

Supports comparison operators `eq`, `in`.

Operator semantics:

- `eq` — Exact match. Default when no operator prefix is supplied.
- `in` — Matches any value in a comma-separated list.

Query examples:

`filter[client.id]=0d3e7d0k-241a-461r-av15-758a90d70283`

`filter[client.id]=eq:0d3e7d0k-241a-461r-av15-758a90d70283`

`filter[client.id]=in:0d3e7d0k-241a-461r-av15-758a90d70283,1a2b3c4d-5e6f-7a8b-9c0d-e1f2a3b4c5d6`

parameters.name: filter[starts_at]
parameters.description:
Filters records by using a query string on the field `starts_at`.

Supports comparison operators `eq`, `gt`, `gte`, `lt`, `lte`.

Operator semantics:

- `eq` — Exact match. Default when no operator prefix is supplied.
- `gt` — Greater than the supplied value.
- `gte` — Greater than or equal to the supplied value.
- `lt` — Less than the supplied value.
- `lte` — Less than or equal to the supplied value.

Query examples:

`filter[starts_at]=2025-11-11T15:30:00Z`

`filter[starts_at]=eq:2025-11-11T15:30:00Z`

`filter[starts_at]=gt:2025-11-11T15:30:00Z`

`filter[starts_at]=gte:2025-11-11T15:30:00Z`

`filter[starts_at]=lt:2025-11-11T15:30:00Z`

`filter[starts_at]=lte:2025-11-11T15:30:00Z`

parameters.name: filter[ends_at]
parameters.description:
Filters records by using a query string on the field `ends_at`.

Supports comparison operators `eq`, `gt`, `gte`, `lt`, `lte`.

Operator semantics:

- `eq` — Exact match. Default when no operator prefix is supplied.
- `gt` — Greater than the supplied value.
- `gte` — Greater than or equal to the supplied value.
- `lt` — Less than the supplied value.
- `lte` — Less than or equal to the supplied value.

Query examples:

`filter[ends_at]=2025-11-11T15:30:00Z`

`filter[ends_at]=eq:2025-11-11T15:30:00Z`

`filter[ends_at]=gt:2025-11-11T15:30:00Z`

`filter[ends_at]=gte:2025-11-11T15:30:00Z`

`filter[ends_at]=lt:2025-11-11T15:30:00Z`

`filter[ends_at]=lte:2025-11-11T15:30:00Z`

parameters.name: filter[is_complete]
parameters.description:
Filters records by using a query string on the field `is_complete`.

Supports comparison operators `eq`.

Operator semantics:

- `eq` — Exact match. Default when no operator prefix is supplied.

Query examples:

`filter[is_complete]=true`

`filter[is_complete]=eq:true`

parameters.name: filter[status]
parameters.description:
Filters records by using a query string on the field `status`.

Supports comparison operators `eq`, `in`.

Operator semantics:

- `eq` — Exact match. Default when no operator prefix is supplied.
- `in` — Matches any value in a comma-separated list.

Query examples:

`filter[status]=example_string`

`filter[status]=eq:example_string`

`filter[status]=in:example_string,another_string`

Available values: `Upcoming`, `OverDue`, `Completed`.

parameters.name: filter[title]
parameters.description:
Filters records by using a query string on the field `title`.

Supports comparison operators `eq`, `cont`.

Operator semantics:

- `eq` — Exact match. Default when no operator prefix is supplied.
- `cont` — Case-insensitive substring match (`LIKE %value%`). Use this for free-form search inputs; the supplied value is matched anywhere inside the field, and `%` / `_` characters in the value are escaped so they do not act as wildcards.

Query examples:

`filter[title]=example_string`

`filter[title]=eq:example_string`

`filter[title]=cont:exam`

parameters.description: Searches meeting titles and client names using a case-insensitive partial match.

parameters.name: filter[assigned_user_id]
parameters.description:
Narrows the list to meetings whose client has one of the supplied users as an Account Owner. Use eq
for one user or in for multiple users. Values are ScalePad Hub user ids or obfuscated user ids; a
user the account does not have is rejected, while a user who exists but owns no client matches
nothing and returns an empty page. The reserved value none matches clients with no Account Owner,
and can appear in an in list alongside user ids to match either. Deactivated users are never
Account Owners. Requires Client Focus access.


An Account Owner is an account team member holding the a primary account team role on that client,
the same rule the account_owners field and the account_owner sort use. This deliberately differs
from the identically named filter on the Clients endpoint, which matches a team member of any role
and whose none means no team member at all.

parameters.name: include_attendees
parameters.description: Whether to return each meeting's attendees in `attendees`. Defaults to false.

parameters.name: filter[client.segment_id]
parameters.description:
Narrows results to clients in any supplied segment. Repeat eq: for each segment, or use in: with a
comma-separated list. Use null:true to match clients with no segment; combined with ids it matches either.

parameters.name: filter[client.vertical_id]
parameters.description:
Narrows results to clients in any supplied vertical. Repeat eq: for each vertical, or use in: with a
comma-separated list. Use null:true to match clients with no vertical; combined with ids it matches either.

parameters.name: filter[client.client_access_group_id]
parameters.description:
Narrows results to clients in any supplied client access group. Repeat eq: for each group, or use in: with
a comma-separated list. Use null:true to match clients with no access group; combined with ids it matches
either.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description:
One or more sortable fields, separated by commas. Prefix with '+' to sort ascending or '-' to sort descending.

Available fields: account_owner, starts_at, title

parameters.name: filter[client.id]
parameters.description:
Filters records by using a query string on the field `client.id`.

Supports comparison operators `eq`.

Operator semantics:

- `eq` — Exact match. Default when no operator prefix is supplied.

Query examples:

`filter[client.id]=0d3e7d0k-241a-461r-av15-758a90d70283`

`filter[client.id]=eq:0d3e7d0k-241a-461r-av15-758a90d70283`

parameters.name: filter[is_archived]
parameters.description:
Filters records by using a query string on the field `is_archived`.

Supports comparison operators `eq`.

Operator semantics:

- `eq` — Exact match. Default when no operator prefix is supplied.

Query examples:

`filter[is_archived]=true`

`filter[is_archived]=eq:true`

parameters.name: filter[client.segment_id]
parameters.description:
Narrows results to clients in any supplied segment. Repeat eq: for each segment, or use in: with a
comma-separated list. Use null:true to match clients with no segment; combined with ids it matches either.

parameters.name: filter[client.vertical_id]
parameters.description:
Narrows results to clients in any supplied vertical. Repeat eq: for each vertical, or use in: with a
comma-separated list. Use null:true to match clients with no vertical; combined with ids it matches either.

parameters.name: filter[client.client_access_group_id]
parameters.description:
Narrows results to clients in any supplied client access group. Repeat eq: for each group, or use in: with
a comma-separated list. Use null:true to match clients with no access group; combined with ids it matches
either.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description:
One or more sortable fields, separated by commas. Prefix with '+' to sort ascending or '-' to sort descending.

Available fields: created_at, title, updated_at

parameters.name: page_size
parameters.description: The number of records to be returned in a single page

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description:
Opaque cursor of the page to return. Omit this value for the first
page, then pass the next_cursor value from the previous response.
            
- Cursor pagination cannot guarantee atomicity.
- Endpoints may skip new records inserted between paginated reads.
- Endpoints may occasionally return duplicate records.

parameters.name: filter[client.id]
parameters.description:
Filters records by using a query string on the field `client.id`.

Supports comparison operators `eq`, `in`.

Operator semantics:

- `eq` — Exact match. Default when no operator prefix is supplied.
- `in` — Matches any value in a comma-separated list.

Query examples:

`filter[client.id]=0d3e7d0k-241a-461r-av15-758a90d70283`

`filter[client.id]=eq:0d3e7d0k-241a-461r-av15-758a90d70283`

`filter[client.id]=in:0d3e7d0k-241a-461r-av15-758a90d70283,1a2b3c4d-5e6f-7a8b-9c0d-e1f2a3b4c5d6`

parameters.name: filter[name]
parameters.description:
Filters records by using a query string on the field `name`.

Supports comparison operators `eq`, `cont`.

Operator semantics:

- `eq` — Exact match. Default when no operator prefix is supplied.
- `cont` — Case-insensitive substring match (`LIKE %value%`). Use this for free-form search inputs; the supplied value is matched anywhere inside the field, and `%` / `_` characters in the value are escaped so they do not act as wildcards.

Query examples:

`filter[name]=example_string`

`filter[name]=eq:example_string`

`filter[name]=cont:exam`

parameters.name: filter[status]
parameters.description:
Filters records by using a query string on the field `status`.

Supports comparison operators `eq`, `in`.

Operator semantics:

- `eq` — Exact match. Default when no operator prefix is supplied.
- `in` — Matches any value in a comma-separated list.

Query examples:

`filter[status]=example_string`

`filter[status]=eq:example_string`

`filter[status]=in:example_string,another_string`

Available values: `Unknown`, `Draft`, `Expired`, `Lost`, `Published`, `SentClicked`, `SentDelivered`, `SentOpened`, `SentPending`, `SentUndeliverable`, `WonAccepted`, `WonFulfilled`, `WonOrdered`.

parameters.name: filter[client.segment_id]
parameters.description:
Narrows results to clients in any supplied segment. Repeat eq: for each segment, or use in: with a
comma-separated list. Use null:true to match clients with no segment; combined with ids it matches either.

parameters.name: filter[client.vertical_id]
parameters.description:
Narrows results to clients in any supplied vertical. Repeat eq: for each vertical, or use in: with a
comma-separated list. Use null:true to match clients with no vertical; combined with ids it matches either.

parameters.name: filter[client.client_access_group_id]
parameters.description:
Narrows results to clients in any supplied client access group. Repeat eq: for each group, or use in: with
a comma-separated list. Use null:true to match clients with no access group; combined with ids it matches
either.

parameters.name: filter[client.id]
parameters.description:
Filters records by using a query string on the field `client.id`.

Supports comparison operators `eq`, `in`.

Operator semantics:

- `eq` — Exact match. Default when no operator prefix is supplied.
- `in` — Matches any value in a comma-separated list.

Query examples:

`filter[client.id]=0d3e7d0k-241a-461r-av15-758a90d70283`

`filter[client.id]=eq:0d3e7d0k-241a-461r-av15-758a90d70283`

`filter[client.id]=in:0d3e7d0k-241a-461r-av15-758a90d70283,1a2b3c4d-5e6f-7a8b-9c0d-e1f2a3b4c5d6`

parameters.name: filter[client.segment_id]
parameters.description:
Narrows results to clients in any supplied segment. Repeat eq: for each segment, or use in: with a
comma-separated list. Use null:true to match clients with no segment; combined with ids it matches either.

parameters.name: filter[client.vertical_id]
parameters.description:
Narrows results to clients in any supplied vertical. Repeat eq: for each vertical, or use in: with a
comma-separated list. Use null:true to match clients with no vertical; combined with ids it matches either.

parameters.name: filter[client.client_access_group_id]
parameters.description:
Narrows results to clients in any supplied client access group. Repeat eq: for each group, or use in: with
a comma-separated list. Use null:true to match clients with no access group; combined with ids it matches
either.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description:
One or more sortable fields, separated by commas. Prefix with '+' to sort ascending or '-' to sort descending.

Available fields: status, client_name, product_name, capacity, utilized

parameters.name: page_size
parameters.description: The number of records to be returned in a single page

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description:
Opaque cursor of the page to return. Omit this value for the first
page, then pass the next_cursor value from the previous response.
            
- Cursor pagination cannot guarantee atomicity.
- Endpoints may skip new records inserted between paginated reads.
- Endpoints may occasionally return duplicate records.

get.description: Get account-wide SaaS portfolio totals and per-client summaries. Pass include_non_paid=false for totals that describe purchased licensing only, excluding trials and intrinsically free entitlements.

parameters.name: include_non_paid
parameters.description:
Whether trials and intrinsically free entitlements contribute to the portfolio totals.
Defaults to true, which counts every asset. Pass false for totals that describe purchasable
seats only; filter[is_paid]=true on the asset list endpoint reproduces that population.
Independently of this parameter, assets Microsoft reported with an uncapped capacity
sentinel are always counted in asset_count, client_count, and product_count, but never
contribute capacity or availability, because their reported capacity is a sentinel rather
than a seat count.

parameters.name: filter[client.segment_id]

parameters.name: filter[client.client_access_group_id]

parameters.name: filter[client.id]
parameters.description:
Filters records by using a query string on the field `client.id`.

Supports comparison operators `eq`, `in`.

Operator semantics:

- `eq` — Exact match. Default when no operator prefix is supplied.
- `in` — Matches any value in a comma-separated list.

Query examples:

`filter[client.id]=0d3e7d0k-241a-461r-av15-758a90d70283`

`filter[client.id]=eq:0d3e7d0k-241a-461r-av15-758a90d70283`

`filter[client.id]=in:0d3e7d0k-241a-461r-av15-758a90d70283,1a2b3c4d-5e6f-7a8b-9c0d-e1f2a3b4c5d6`

parameters.name: filter[is_completed]
parameters.description:
Filters records by using a query string on the field `is_completed`.

Supports comparison operators `eq`.

Operator semantics:

- `eq` — Exact match. Default when no operator prefix is supplied.

Query examples:

`filter[is_completed]=true`

`filter[is_completed]=eq:true`

parameters.name: filter[is_overdue]
parameters.description:
Filters records by using a query string on the field `is_overdue`.

Supports comparison operators `eq`.

Operator semantics:

- `eq` — Exact match. Default when no operator prefix is supplied.

Query examples:

`filter[is_overdue]=true`

`filter[is_overdue]=eq:true`

parameters.name: filter[status]
parameters.description:
Filters records by using a query string on the field `status`.

Supports comparison operators `eq`, `in`.

Operator semantics:

- `eq` — Exact match. Default when no operator prefix is supplied.
- `in` — Matches any value in a comma-separated list.

Query examples:

`filter[status]=example_string`

`filter[status]=eq:example_string`

`filter[status]=in:example_string,another_string`

Available values: `Upcoming`, `Overdue`, `Completed`.

parameters.name: timezone
parameters.description:
IANA timezone the statuses are evaluated in, deciding when a due day has ended.
A task is Upcoming throughout its due day in this timezone and Overdue once that day
ends. Defaults to UTC when omitted.

parameters.name: search

parameters.description: The unique identifier of the client whose tickets should be returned.

parameters.description: The maximum number of tickets to return.

parameters.description: The opaque cursor returned by the previous page.

parameters.name: filter[external_id]
parameters.description:
Restrict results to the given PSA ticket numbers, matched exactly. Use this to look up a known
ticket instead of paging the client's whole ticket list.

parameters.name: filter[board_name]
parameters.description: Restrict results to the given PSA boards or queues, matched exactly by name.

parameters.name: filter[status]
parameters.description:
Restrict results to the given ScalePad-standardized ticket statuses, matched exactly. These are
ScalePad's normalized statuses, not the connected PSA's own status labels — for example NEW,
IN_PROGRESS, or CLOSED. The set is owned by Core and can grow, so values are passed through rather
than checked against a list here; a status Core does not recognize simply matches no tickets.

get.description:
Returns one row per app the client has usage data for in the reporting period, with usage metrics, certifications, and lifecycle classification. This is the data backing the SaaS Management app dashboard.

`sort` accepts canonical_name, unique_users, active_time, avg_time, or session_count, with a `-` prefix for descending order; defaults to canonical_name ascending.

`filter[app_id]`, `filter[user_id]`, `filter[department_id]`, `filter[category_id]`, `filter[vendor_id]`, `filter[approval_status]`, `filter[is_favorite]`, and `filter[lifecycle]` narrow the result set — see the filter parameter description for operator support per field. `filter[user_id]` and `filter[department_id]` additionally restrict unique_users, avg_time_ms_per_day, and session_count to activity from the given user(s)/department; an app with no matching activity is omitted rather than returned with zeroed metrics.

`q` searches by app name. `has_compliance_gap`, `missing_frameworks`, and `compliance_frameworks` filter on certification status.

Pagination is cursor-based and best-effort/non-atomic: rows may be skipped or duplicated between page requests if the underlying data changes concurrently.

get.description:
Returns one bucket per `granularity` unit over the date range, with a count of apps in each of five mutually-exclusive, priority-ordered lifecycle segments for that bucket:

1. `risky_apps` — scanned with a compliance gap (missing a required framework). Top priority: a risky app is never also counted in another segment.
2. `unapproved_apps` — not risky, and explicitly marked not approved.
3. `ai_apps` — not risky, and categorized as an AI app.
4. `other_apps` — not risky, approved, not AI, and had activity in the bucket.
5. `unused_apps` — not risky, approved, not AI, with prior usage but no activity in the bucket.

Apps with an unreviewed approval status are excluded from every segment. `filter[department_id]` and `filter[approval_status]` (both list, `in` operator) scope which apps are counted.

This endpoint has no comparison period (`period.compare_start_date` / `compare_end_date` are always null) and no pagination — all buckets in the range are returned in a single response.

replacement.description:
Estimated cost to replace this asset, in whole units of the budget currency of the asset's client.
Carries the per-asset override when one is set and per-asset replacement cost is enabled for the account,
and otherwise the replacement value in effect for the asset's type. Null when no asset type could be resolved for the device, which is not the same as the
device having none - `category` may still be populated from the reported hardware type. No
currency code is returned here; read it for the same client from
`GET /v1/assets/types or GET /v1/clients/{client_id}/types`, which denominates the type-level replacement
values this field shadows.

the report. A custom scheduled report has no equivalent.

client_id.description:
Client scoping filter. Use `eq` for one client id or `in`
for multiple client ids.

name_filter.description: Agreement name filter. Use the `cont` operator to match the agreement name or display name.

is_hidden_filters.description:
Hidden agreement filter. Use `eq` for one hidden state or `in`
for multiple hidden states. Defaults to false when omitted.

statuses.description:
Agreement status filter. Use `eq` for one status or `in`
for multiple statuses. Available values: Active, Inactive.

cost_types.description:
Billing cost type filter. Use `eq` for one cost type or
`in` for multiple cost types. Available values: Actual, Estimate.

billing_cycles.description:
Billing cycle filter. Use `eq` for one billing cycle or
`in` for multiple billing cycles.
Available values: Monthly, Quarterly, Annually, SemiAnnual, EveryTwoYears, EveryThreeYears, EveryFourYears, EveryFiveYears, EveryTenYears, OneTime, BiMonthly, Unknown, BiWeekly.

location.description:
Agreement location filter. Use `eq` for one location or `in`
for multiple locations.

is_third_party.description:
Third-party agreement filter. Use the `eq` operator with
`true` or `false`.

auto_renew.description:
Auto-renew filter applied to the list query or export. Query requests
use the `eq` operator.
Available values: Yes, No, Either.

expiry_filters.description:
Renewal or expiry windows applied to the list or export. Query requests
use `filter[expiry]` with `eq` for one window or `in` for multiple windows.
Available values: Expired, ZeroToThirty, ThirtyOneToSixty, SixtyOneToNinety, NinetyPlus.

is_expired_filters.description:
Expired agreement filter. Agreements without a renewal or end date are not expired.
Defaults to no constraint when omitted.

sort.description:
One or more sortable fields, separated by commas. Prefix with `+`
for ascending or `-` for descending.
Available values: billing_next_due_at, end_at, name, client.name, billing_cost_subunits, status, billing_cycle, is_auto_renew.

period.description:
The initiative's own schedule window. Null dates indicate the initiative is unscheduled.
Both dates are inclusive calendar dates carried in a date-time field, always midnight UTC, so
compare them as calendar dates. Converting them to a local zone shifts the day west of UTC
(2026-06-30T00:00:00Z reads as Jun 29), and an end-date range check must be inclusive of that
whole day rather than a "less than or equal to midnight" comparison against a date plus time.

record_created_at.description:
When this initiative record was created (ISO-8601 UTC). Null when the record's
timestamps are unavailable (for example, an initiative removed between forecast
computation and detail lookup).

record_updated_at.description:
When this initiative record was last updated (ISO-8601 UTC). Null on the same
terms as record_created_at.

primary team member, ordered by display name with the account-team-member id as a final
tiebreak so the order is stable across page loads. Deactivated users are never
eligible, and there is no fallback to other roles, so a client with team members but no

give the total. Returned only when `include_attendees` is true.

SaasManagementAppDashboardItemWithUsers.description: Same shape as SaasManagementAppDashboardItem, plus the app's top users by average time.

app.description: The app this row is for.

unique_users.description: Distinct users who used this app in the period.

active_time_ms.description: Total active time across all users, in milliseconds.

avg_time_ms_per_day.description: Average active time per day, in milliseconds.

usage_level.description: Usage intensity classification, or null when there is insufficient data to classify.

risk_level.description: Risk classification, or null for approved apps.

compliance_scanned.description: Whether the app has been scanned for compliance (has at least one current compliance assertion). An unscanned app is never flagged with a compliance gap.

compliance_gap.description: True when the app is scanned and missing at least one of the client's required compliance frameworks. Always false for an unscanned app.

missing_frameworks.description: Required frameworks the app lacks a current self-declared alignment for. Empty when the app is unscanned or has no gap.

users.description: Top users of this app by average time, capped at users_limit (default 50, max 200).

SaasManagementAppDashboardResponse.description: App dashboard rows for a client, wrapped with pagination metadata.

SaasManagementAppDashboardTimeseriesPoin.description: App lifecycle segment counts for one granularity bucket.

risky_apps.description: Scanned apps with a compliance gap. Top-priority segment; a risky app is excluded from every other segment.

unused_apps.description: Approved, non-AI apps with prior usage but no activity in this bucket.

other_apps.description: Approved, non-AI, non-risky apps with activity in this bucket.

SaasManagementAppDashboardTimeseriesPoin.description: The pointed lifecycle segment counts. This endpoint has no cursor pagination — every point in the range is always returned.

data.description: One entry per granularity unit in the range.

SaasManagementAppDashboardTimeseriesResp.description: An app lifecycle timeseries for a client — one entry per granularity unit.

period.description: The resolved reporting period. compare_start_date/compare_end_date are always null — this endpoint has no comparison period.

SaasManagementAppDashboardUser.description: One user's usage of a given app within the reporting period.

user.description: The user this entry is for.

avg_time_ms_per_day.description: This user's average active time per day on the app, in milliseconds.

days_active.description: Distinct days this user was active on the app in the period.

SaasManagementAppDashboardWithUsersAppsP.description: A page of app dashboard rows, each with its top users embedded, with cursor-pagination metadata.

data.description: Per-app dashboard rows, each with its top users.

total_count.description: Total number of rows matching the query, across all pages.

next_cursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page, or null on the last page. Pass the value back unmodified.

SaasManagementAppDashboardWithUsersRespo.description: App dashboard rows for a client, each with its top users embedded, wrapped with pagination metadata.

apps.description: Paginated app dashboard rows, each with its top users.

SaasManagementCatalogAppRef.description: The shared catalog application backing a client's app row: name, logo, vendor, categories, and compliance certifications.

id.description: Catalog application identifier.

logo.description: URL to the application logo, or null if unavailable.

type.description: Application type, or null if unclassified.

categories.description: Catalog categories the application belongs to.

compliance_assertions.description: Current compliance assertions for this application. Always present, may be empty even for a scanned app with no findings — use the endpoint-specific compliance_scanned field to distinguish a clean scan from an unscanned app.

SaasManagementCatalogCategory.description: A catalog category an application is classified under.

id.description: Category identifier.

name.description: Category name.

SaasManagementCatalogVendor.description: The vendor that publishes a catalog application.

id.description: Vendor identifier.

name.description: Vendor name.

url.description: Vendor website URL, or null if unknown.

SaasManagementComplianceAssertionRef.description: One normalized compliance-framework assertion discovered for a catalog application. At most one current assertion is returned per framework.

id.description: Assertion identifier.

framework.description: Compliance framework the assertion is about.

status.description: Normalized status of the claim.

SaasManagementEnrollmentToken.description: An enrollment token, including its one-time-visible credential value.

id.description: Stable unique identifier for the enrollment token.

value.description: One-time-visible device-enrollment credential. The enrolling RMM/Core agent presents this value to a separate device-enrollment endpoint to register a device under this client.

description.description: Human-readable label for the token.
description.example: Front office rollout

site_id.description: Optional site identifier the token is scoped to.

status.description: Token status.

max_uses.description: Maximum number of uses, or null for unlimited.

remaining_uses.description: Remaining uses, or null for unlimited.

expires_at.description: Expiry timestamp, or null if the token does not expire.

SaasManagementEnrollmentTokenCreateReque.description: Request body for creating a client enrollment token.

description.description: Human-readable label for the token.
description.example: Front office rollout

site_id.description: Optional site identifier the token is scoped to.

expires_at.description: Expiry date (YYYY-MM-DD), stored as end-of-day UTC. Omit for a token that never expires until revoked.

SaasManagementError.description: A single error entry describing one reason a request failed.

code.description: Machine-readable error code identifying the failure type.

title.description: Short, human-readable summary of the error.

detail.description: Detailed explanation of the error and how to resolve it.
detail.example: The request could not be processed. Please ensure that the request follows the API specification in the documentation.

SaasManagementErrorResponse.description: Error envelope returned when a request cannot be processed. Carries one or more error entries.

errors.description: List of errors describing why the request failed.

example.title: Bad Request
example.detail: The request could not be processed. Please ensure that the request follows the API specification in the documentation.

SaasManagementMetricWithDelta.description: A numeric metric paired with its change against an optional comparison period. compare_value and change_value/change_pct are null when no comparison period was requested.

value.description: Metric value for the primary period.

change_pct.description: Percentage change versus the comparison period.

compare_value.description: Raw metric value for the comparison period.

change_value.description: Absolute change versus the comparison period.

SaasManagementNullableMetricWithDelta.description: Same shape as SaasManagementMetricWithDelta, but value itself may also be null (used for averages that are undefined when there is no underlying data).

value.description: Metric value for the primary period, or null when there is insufficient data.

change_pct.description: Percentage change versus the comparison period.

compare_value.description: Raw metric value for the comparison period.

change_value.description: Absolute change versus the comparison period.

SaasManagementUserLastActivity.description: The most recent activity timestamps for a user, broken out by channel.

at.description: Most recent activity across any channel, or null if the user has never been active.

desktop_at.description: Most recent desktop-agent activity, or null.

web_at.description: Most recent web activity, or null.

SaasManagementUserRef.description: A lightweight reference to a client user.

id.description: User identifier.

user_key.description: User key, typically an email address.

SaasManagementUtilizationSummary.description: SaaS-utilization summary metrics for a client over the reporting period.

total_apps_used.description: Number of apps with activity in the period.

unapproved_app_count.description: Number of approved-state apps explicitly marked not approved.

ai_app_count.description: Number of approved apps categorized as AI.

total_active_time_ms.description: Total active time across all apps in the period, in milliseconds.
